paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: you can bring God everything, even the ugly parts. This prayer doesn't dress anything up. It remembers His goodness, admits "Surely You were angry, for we sinned," and says even their best acts are "like filthy rags" (Isaiah 64:5-6). And they still keep talking to Him the whole way through.

Now look at where the prayer lands. After all that confessing, it says, "But now, O LORD, You are our Father; we are the clay, and You are the potter; we are all the work of Your hand" (Isaiah 64:8). They don't say "we earned it." They say "You are our Father." I think that's the whole lesson right there: we can't fix ourselves, but we belong to a Father who made us.

So when you're worn out, or you've blown it, or the ruins are all you can see, do what this prayer does. Remember who He has been, tell Him the truth, and ask Him to come near. I know a little about being stuck in the dark, friend, and I can tell you the One who reaches in is the One who made you. Keep your hands open, because the potter isn't finished with the clay.
